incident.description: A new deployment introduces a bug in order total calculation, causing ~35% of /orders and /orders/{id} requests to fail with a 500.

change_analysis_agent.interpretation: I'll investigate the recent deployment history to identify the change most likely related to this incident.The most recent change, chg-004 (deployment `1.2.0-bad` on 2026-10-13), is described as "refactored order total calculation" — directly matching the reported bug in order total calculation affecting /orders endpoints. It is the newest change by a wide margin (nearly a month after chg-003), making it the prime suspect.

metrics_agent.interpretation: I'll gather the actual metrics before interpreting.Metrics show GET /orders and GET /orders/1 each at 6/15 = 40% error rate (12 of the 40 total requests, 12 total errors), while /health, /changes, and /logs have zero errors. Latency is not the issue — the failing order endpoints are actually the fastest (p99 0.68 ms and 0.69 ms), so this looks like a functional/500-style failure rather than a performance problem.

database_agent.interpretation:
I'll investigate the database health to look for evidence relevant to this incident.The database itself looks healthy: the `orders` table holds 10 rows (6 completed, 3 pending, 1 failed), and all recent queries are simple SELECTs returning correct row counts with sub-millisecond timings (avg 0.02 ms across 18 queries) — no slow queries, errors, or connection issues are visible.

This is consistent with the reported bug: the failures are in application-layer order total calculation, not the database, since reads complete quickly and successfully at the DB level. Note the tool doesn't capture application error rates, so a ~35% request failure rate producing 500s would occur after a successful query, and the "1 failed" order status is not necessarily related.

logs_traces_agent.observation: query_logs({'level': 'ERROR', 'limit': 100}) -> ok=True, fields=['entries', 'count']; query_logs({'limit': 100}) -> ok=True, fields=['entries', 'count']; get_trace({'trace_id': '4e2b567d28c14b6c'}) -> ok=True, fields=['trace']; get_trace({'trace_id': '7edd7b0391084502'}) -> ok=True, fields=['trace']
logs_traces_agent.interpretation:
I'll investigate the logs and traces for evidence.I have strong log evidence. Let me examine one failing trace and one succeeding trace.## Findings

**Logs:** 12 ERROR entries, all at 2026-10-13T18:18:10Z, exclusively on `GET /orders` and `GET /orders/1`, all returning 500. Every one carries the identical message: `OrderServiceError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'total'`. The mixed INFO/ERROR stream shows these failures are interleaved with successful 200s on the same paths (e.g. trace `7edd7b0391084502` GET /orders/1 returned 200), consistent with intermittent (~1/3) failure. The error is fast (0.34–0.65 ms), not a timeout — an immediate code-level exception, and the message points to total calculation dereferencing a `None` value.

**Traces:** The failing trace (`4e2b567d28c14b6c`, /orders/1, 500) and a succeeding counterpart (`7edd7b0391084502`, /orders/1, 200) record only request-level metadata; no additional spans or stack detail are exposed. `/health` and `/changes` continue to return 200.

**Interpretation:** The logs directly corroborate the reported bug: intermittent 500s on `/orders` and `/orders/{id}` caused by `OrderServiceError: 'NoneType' object has no attribute 'total'`, i.e. the order-total calculation fails when it receives a None. Traces add no span-level detail beyond confirming a mix of 500 and 200 responses on the same endpoint.

hypotheses.statement: The incident is caused by the deployment of version 1.2.0-bad at 2026-10-13T18:18:08Z ('refactored order total calculation'), which introduced a bad code change that intermittently dereferences a None order total ("'NoneType' object has no attribute 'total'"), producing fast 500 errors on GET /orders and GET /orders/1 while other endpoints remain healthy.
missing_evidence: Commit diff or release notes for chg-004 / version 1.2.0-bad showing the order total calculation change
Before/after error-rate comparison across the 18:18:08Z deployment boundary to confirm onset coincides with the deploy
Source-level stack trace for the OrderServiceError to confirm the None dereference originates in the refactored total calculation
hypotheses.requested_next_investigation: Inspect the code change in deployment 1.2.0-bad (chg-004) covering the order total calculation and roll it back or fix the None handling.

hypotheses.statement: The 500 errors on /orders endpoints stem from a code-level defect in OrderService total calculation that receives a null/None order total, causing an immediate application exception rather than a performance or database problem, as evidenced by fast failures (0.34-0.65 ms) that occur after successful sub-millisecond DB queries.
missing_evidence: Application source code for the order total calculation and its null-handling logic
Input data identifying which orders produce a None total (e.g., orders with missing line items or status)
Confirmation that the DB queries returning rows are the same requests that subsequently fail in the app layer
hypotheses.requested_next_investigation: Trace the OrderService code path from successful DB query to the None-type failure in total calculation.

unsupported_assumptions: That the None dereference specifically originates in the refactored total calculation rather than anywhere else in the order rendering path touched by the deploy
That the error is 'intermittent' by exact code branch rather than dependent on which specific order records (e.g., orders lacking a total) are requested
That the pre-deploy period had zero comparable error rates -- no before-onset metrics were inspected
That the 500s began exactly at the 18:18:08Z deploy boundary; the earliest observed error is 18:18:10Z and there is no pre-deploy baseline in the pool
alternative_explanations: A data problem: one or more order records have a null/missing total, and the new code path surfaces the resulting NoneType error only for those records (the DB shows orders with status failed/pending that could plausibly lack totals), independent of any code defect in the refactor itself
A configuration/state inconsistency introduced alongside the deploy rather than the code change itself, though no config change appears near the deploy time
A latent bug pre-existing in 1.1.0 that was only exposed by the new code path or by the current order data set
requested_evidence: Endpoint error-rate/latency metrics for a window before 18:18:08Z (e.g., pre-deploy) vs after, to confirm a step change in /orders error rate coinciding with the deploy
Deployment/release notes or change detail for chg-004 describing exactly what the 'refactored order total calculation' changed (the reachable change-history field for that deploy)
critic_results.rationale: The only deployment in the incident window (chg-004, v1.2.0-bad, 18:18:08Z) immediately precedes the first 500s at 18:18:10Z; all 12 errors are concentrated on /orders and /orders/1 with a single consistent NoneType 'total' error, while /health, /changes and /logs are clean and DB queries are fast (~0.02ms), so a backend/DB-infrastructure cause is ruled out. The successful 200s at the same time are the normal partial-failure signature and do not contradict the hypothesis.
